writer_notes: IN HOUSE: Add the Elf's spoken dialogue after the adventurer lands on the cottage and the Elf sees the destroyed ceiling.
GATE BACKGROUND: Add the Elf's spoken dialogue at the gate.
AFTER THE ELF LEAVES: Stage direction: the Elf leaves and the Fae appears before the adventurer. Then add the Fae's spoken dialogue.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You are a lone adventurer that was traveling to the Capital to make some money. Unfortunately, you’ve strayed from the main path and ended up completely lost. Even worse, when you were walking through the forest, you got captured by a giant snake. Luckily, it loses interest in you after realizing that you were human, but it still throws you away, sending you off flying. You eventually land on top of a small cottage. You’re alive and well, but the house’s ceiling is completely destroyed and in front of you is a very angry looking elf.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Do you have any idea what you’ve done? You’ve fallen straight through the roof of my home!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He looks up and down at you, clearly still rattled and confused.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: I don’t know how you feel through my roof, but you clearly don’t seem to be from these parts, you at least deserve an explanation. You are in an enchanted grove, a place I have lived in and protected for centuries. Once, it was thriving, beautiful, and full of life, but its condition has gradually deteriorated over the years. I have done everything I can to restore it, but perhaps now I could use your help.

lines.speaker: elf
lines.text: Unfortunately, you cannot simply leave. The only way out is through that gate, and it has been sealed with three locks. I will unlock one lock for every task you complete for me. I know this is not where you intended to end up, but perhaps your arrival can do some good after all. For now, get some rest, and come speak to me tomorrow. I will tell you what needs to be done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A soft voice suddenly whispered from behind you.

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: Oh, don’t mind him. He’s always like that—so serious, so self-important. Honestly, I don’t know how anyone can stand listening to him talk about this grove for hours.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A fae stepped out from behind a tree, smiling warmly.

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: I heard what he said to you, and I couldn’t help but feel sorry for you. Trapped here, forced to run errands for an elf you barely know… it hardly seems fair, does it?

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: But there’s another way out. You don’t need to do his little tasks or wait for him to unlock those gates. I know how we can break the locks ourselves. If you help me, we can both escape this place and go wherever we please. You could finally return to your world, and I could… well, I have a few things I’d like to take care of there myself.

lines.speaker: fae
lines.text: You don’t have to trust him just because he claims to be protecting this grove. Help me instead. I promise, I only want to help you get home. Just… think about it, alright? You don’t have to decide right now. But when you do, come find me. We could both be free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With one last smile, the fae slipped back into the trees.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You’ve had a long day of dealing with mythical creatures. There’s so much to deal with, but you’re too tired to think about it. You set up your sleeping bag and quickly nod off to sleep.
